changes: Rent ramp beat: 485 MW billing against 437 MW in mid-July and 395 MW in June; colocation revenue $215.4mn, +58% QoQ; colocation gross margin 60%.
First clean operating profit: operating income $72.4mn (31% margin) against a $78.5mn loss, with adjusted EBITDA margin 57%.

AMD funding still open: the 10-Q says the build will need additional external financing, with project bonds expected within 12 months and 'no assurance'. Management says no equity is expected for the initial 530 MW and all its equity is already invested.
Liquidity fell $857mn to $1,744mn after $540mn of capex and $444mn for Polaris, against $4.4bn of purchase and construction commitments, mostly over 24 months.
Definition correction: the $3bn market-cap test is a condition to borrow on the revolver, not a maintenance covenant. The quarterly test is $150mn minimum liquidity.
checks: Dates on EDGAR: 8-K item 2.02 (12:04 UTC) and 10-Q (13:09 UTC) on 5 November; release and 10-Q read directly. Call: full MarketBeat/Quartr transcript read once by a research agent; a fresh verifier could not reopen it (preview page only), so key points were spot-checked against BigGo's AI summary: air permits, no equity, $650mn warrants, 2027 deadlines, Dalton, 385 MW and analyst names all matched; firm attributions and ratings are not independently confirmed, and no CoreWeave question appears in either. Consensus from the preview record and MarketBeat. Derived numbers computed in Python. Fresh subagent checked the draft; corrections applied (AMD construction status, warrant-cash wording, converts). Price intraday at 9:57 ET; full-day reaction not available. No bond quote found. 10-Q covenant wording corrects the prior scorecard note.
consensus_thesis: Investors own Core Scientific as a colocation landlord with about 1.1 GW leased, moving from CoreWeave-only to AMD-backed tenancy, and price doubt over CoreWeave credit and over how the $6bn AMD build gets financed.
headline: The consensus view needs little change: delivery and margins came in better than expected, which supports the rent story, but credit quality holds rather than improves until the AMD project bond prices and because almost all current revenue still depends on CoreWeave, whose debt trades at distressed levels.
kona: Three points. A signed AMD-backed lease still has not produced a priced bond after more than three months, so Kona should not assume paper converts to debt quickly. AMD's support came with warrants valued at $90.1mn on the first 530 MW, about $0.17mn per MW, plus more on reserved MW: credit from a stronger party has a price Kona should budget. And US peers now pursue behind-the-meter with air permits unfiled, which keeps Kona's permitted off-grid pitch relevant, though analysts here asked about permits more than anything else.
monitor: First AMD project bond: size, yield, advance rate, recourse.
Dalton Phase Two: the last roughly 100 MW of CoreWeave billing by early 2027, and first Pecos delivery in 1H27.
Tranche 1 warrant cash (about $650mn, expiry 23 January 2027) and whether AMD exercises reservations through 2027.

sections.body: Emphasized more: AMD share of NOI (over half of stabilized NOI on under half of capacity); new power (about 385 MW more at Muskogee and Hunt by mid-2028); behind-the-meter at Pecos; capital scarcity as an advantage ('capital is the throttle on all new development'). Emphasized less or dropped: speculative build of about 500 MW was not quantified; mining exits by year-end. KPIs more important: billing MW, operating margin, liquidity against commitments. Less: net income. Risks up: funding sequence, Texas permits. Down: CoreWeave delivery, cost of mining drag. Margin moves are structural: fixed rent on delivered MW over a mostly fixed cost base.

Next dollar: 7.75% notes (May 2026); no later price. Maturities: $3.30bn 7.75% notes due 2031, amortizing; $460mn 3.00% converts due 2029; $625mn 0% converts due 2031. Market cap about $3.7bn on $11.63 (5 November, 9:57 ET, down 8.9%); the 4 November close of $12.76 was before results. No bond quote found.
